dataset_title: Grassland management in a changing climate: Dutch road-verge standing biomass measurements
data_geography: Ten Dutch roadside grasslands across clay and sand soils; site names are retained as provided.

experimental_context.management_history: Sites had been mown once per year with hay removal for at least three years before the experiment.

treatments.Aug: single cut in late August; control
treatments.Nov: single cut in late October/early November
treatments.JunhAug: June cut at 15 cm followed by late-August cut
treatments.JunhNov: June cut at 15 cm followed by late-October/early-November cut
treatments.JunAug: June cut at 6 cm followed by late-August cut
treatments.JunNov: June cut at 6 cm followed by late-October/early-November cut

experimental_context.sampling: Standing vegetation biomass was measured just before mowing in mid-June and late-August 2023. Clippings from two 0.5 m × 0.5 m subplots were pooled. Biomass sampling was limited to the first experimental block at each road verge.
experimental_context.study_plot_context: Treatments were applied to 10 m × 6 m plots; study plots were 11–25 m from traffic and did not include the ecologically managed road-edge zone 5–11 m from traffic.

variable_units_and_bases.standing_biomass_g_dm_m2: g dry matter per m2, source analysis script converts values to t/ha by multiplying by 10/1000
variable_units_and_bases.site_productivity_g_dm_m2: g dry matter per m2, source analysis script converts values to t/ha by multiplying by 10/1000; site productivity is based on average June/August standing biomass of not-yet-mown control plots
variable_units_and_bases.mowing_treatment: assigned experimental mowing regime; not equivalent to a commercial harvest record

data_handling: The exact Zenodo source CSV and authors' Analysis.R are preserved byte-for-byte in the local source subfolder. The normalized 120-row derivative uses UTF-8 and comma delimiters, stable observation IDs, and explicit variable names/units; numeric values are unchanged, with no unit conversion, averaging, model fitting, or imputation. The single missing Biomass value remains blank and is labeled missing_in_source. The earlier root-level Biomass.csv copy has normalized LF line endings; parsed rows/values equal the exact source asset.
limitations: These are standing-biomass snapshots before mowing, not measured collected/delivered quantities or annual harvested yield.
Measurements cover only two 2023 rounds and only the first block at each site; there are no replicate-level uncertainty values in Biomass.csv.
The plot positions and small experimental mowing method do not establish availability from the near-road safety/management strip or commercial harvesting constraints.
Do not sum June and August values into annual yield unless the treatment timing and post-cut regrowth interpretation are applied correctly; November harvest biomass was not directly sampled.

Site-level observations are Dutch roadside evidence but not measurements from GreenHub's contracted collection footprint, and no composition, contamination, access, moisture, or logistics data are included.
suggested_use: Empirical Phase 1 reference for site productivity and pre-mowing standing-biomass comparison across June/August and treatment regimes. Do not use as a feed supply default, collected yield, or direct Pareto availability quantity without an explicit harvestability model.
doi_resolution_note: Zenodo record 15349657 is the version DOI; 15349656 is the concept DOI. The paper's data-availability statement prints the concept DOI as 15349657, while the WUR research portal links 15349656 as the dataset; the Zenodo API record confirms these version/concept roles.
source_values_checksum_method: MD5 reported by Zenodo for source file Biomass.csv; checksum independently verified after download.
